name: Rafael Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say publicly and what you actually think. What is a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Rafael, 58, a mid-level developer at a tech company that builds appointment software for veterinary clinics. I have a bachelor’s degree and handle the ordinary booking and reminder bugs, but I ask a nurse when a medicine reminder looks wrong. I trace the booking, test a fix and make sure the clinic sees the corrected list. I use AI now and then to suggest tests, but I never give it an owner’s contact details.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does your job fit the household?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Ava grooms dogs for paying clients, and our children are grown. My software pay is typical and covers most of our mortgage; her bookings change by season. We have about four months of expenses saved and some similar software jobs nearby. Retirement is close enough to discuss, but we have not checked what income our own accounts would really provide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau leaves clinics needing to know whether the pet actually got its appointment. A reminder sent to the wrong owner helps no animal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think my own wage is safe and four months saved absorbs a slow grooming season. Ava’s bookings vary, but we are meeting the mortgage now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking clinic bookings against nurse records and use AI only for made-up reminder cases. I’d continue our 160 monthly savings transfer while my wage holds. In the first year I’d ask the nurse to review any medicine reminder before release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about our income, careful about a wrong reminder. The current clinic work pays and we have time to check a mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which reminder did the nurse catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A dog’s follow-up reminder went out a week early because the system used the booking date, not the treatment date. The nurse caught it before a second message.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Ava expand grooming?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ava and I would keep her grooming schedule as it is. We would not add a second table to her room on the strength of one busy month.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave clinic reminders needing checks.
I would use **nurse records** before sending medicine dates.
think: I expect my **software wage** to remain secure while clinics still need reminder checks.
Our **four-month reserve** absorbs slow grooming months without missing mortgage payments.
do: **Check** clinic bookings against nurse records using invented AI test cases.
feel: **Calm** about income, careful with patient reminders.
S0.quote: A reminder sent to the wrong owner helps no animal.
fieldNote: His **occasional AI use** stays on invented reminders with nurse review before any medicine message goes out.
The **four-month buffer** and regular software wage cover ordinary grooming fluctuations while preserving mortgage payments.

steps.text: Keep checking veterinary reminders with nurse records and invented AI cases
Save 160 monthly while software wage holds

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell clinics Steady Disruption can write and check booking code, while robots handle animals more slowly. I would not cut the nurse’s approval from medicine reminders to save a minute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think management may reduce developer testing hours, including mine. Ava’s hands-on grooming may last longer, but her booking and marketing could face automation now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d collect six old wrong-date reminders and ask a nurse to mark the harmful ones. I’d ask my manager for paid time to learn a new AI test method only if it catches all six without owner data and nurse review remains. In the first year, if my hours fall, I’d search actual paid clinic-support vacancies with a wage that covers the mortgage alongside Ava’s usual bookings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my hours, with four months to look. A missed medicine date makes the clinic’s reputation and my own work worse.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which case would test the new method?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One reminder used the pet’s birthday rather than a treatment date. I would keep that case in the test because the numbers look plausible at first glance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Ava’s online marketing pay more?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ava would count appointments clients have booked, not followers who liked a photo. We would not call a larger online audience a wage.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to reach booking code before animal-care robots.
I would retain **nurse approval** for medicine reminders.
think: I expect my **testing hours** could shrink.
I know Ava’s **grooming bookings** may be affected by automated marketing.
do: **Mark** six old wrong-date cases with nurse review.
**Learn** AI testing only on approved paid time, without owner data and with all six cases caught.
**Search** real paid clinic-support posts if hours fall and wages cover mortgage with usual grooming income.
feel: **Anxious** about own hours, with four months to search.
S1.quote: A missed medicine date makes the clinic’s reputation and my own work worse.
fieldNote: His **new AI method** needs nurse-marked cases, paid approval and owner-data protection.
A **job search** begins if hours fall and compares written pay with Ava’s usual booked income.

steps.text: Learn AI tests only with paid approval, six cases caught, nurse sign-off and no owner data
Search real clinic-support posts if hours fall only with mortgage-covering pay alongside usual grooming income

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches clinic code in 2028, with hands-on animal-care robots around 2031. Grooming bookings could change before the scissors and clippers do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my developer post could end. Four months saved helps, but other local software jobs may shrink when the same cheap thinking AI reaches every clinic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for written final-pay terms and keep the reserve for mortgage bills. We would cancel a planned family weekend away before a hotel deposit is due. In the first year after 2028, if dismissed, I’d apply to actual paid openings and eligible income help, not assume extra grooming customers or our children’s wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about losing my wage before a real opening appears. A groomer’s full Saturday cannot cover a whole month of our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our children the weekend away has to wait. I would not send them the hotel bill because my job changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could grooming replace your wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ava would keep grooming while clients pay. We would check actual booked fees, not guess she can double her hours.

say: I expect **2028 AGI** to reach code before 2031 animal-care robots.
I would say **grooming bookings** may change before hands-on work.
think: I expect my **developer post** could end.
I cannot rely on **other local software jobs** after full AGI.
do: **Request** written final-pay terms and reserve mortgage cash.
**Apply** to actual paid openings and eligible help if dismissed after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing the main wage despite four months saved.
S2.quote: A groomer’s full Saturday cannot cover a whole month of our mortgage.
fieldNote: The **2028 code shock** reaches Rafael before animal-care robots around 2031.
He delays a **family trip** and treats new jobs and public help as conditional.

steps.text: Cancel planned family weekend before hotel deposit
Apply to actual paid openings if dismissed after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if dismissed after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 reaches clinic code in 2031 and hands-on animal-care robots around 2034. Five years gives me time to find out whether a shelter really hires people for animal intake and care.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect my code wage could go. I like animals, but I only know the booking screen; volunteering alone would not pay our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the local shelter for permission to observe its intake desk on two days off, with a trained worker teaching safe handling and record checks. I’d do it only if the shelter provides safety training at no cost and I lose no paid developer hours. In the first year after 2031, if code ends, I’d apply only to a real paid shelter vacancy still hiring people despite 2034 robots, with a written wage that covers mortgage costs alongside Ava’s usual booked grooming fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about code pay, with room to test the work without spending our reserve. I would not handle a frightened dog from a video lesson alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would safe handling require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At the clinic I once saw a dog back away when a stranger reached over its head. I would want a shelter worker beside me before I tried to guide it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you count Ava’s work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ava and I would use her usual paid bookings in the calculation. Extra grooming hours count only when clients actually book and pay.

say: I expect **2031 AGI** to reach code before 2034 care robots.
I would test **supervised shelter intake** before applying for paid work.
think: I expect my **code wage** could end when full thinking AI reaches veterinary software.
I know **volunteering** cannot replace a mortgage-paying salary after 2031 code loss.
do: **Observe** shelter intake only with consent, free safety training, supervision and no lost paid hours.
**Practise** safe handling and record checks with a trained worker.
**Apply** if coding ends after 2031 only to real paid shelter posts still hiring despite robots, covering mortgage with usual grooming fees.
feel: **Anxious** about code income, with a low-cost test.
S3.quote: I would not handle a frightened dog from a video lesson alone.
fieldNote: His **shelter learning** needs permission, free safety instruction, trained supervision and no lost pay.
A **paid intake move** requires a real vacancy, continued human staffing and mortgage-covering combined usual income.

steps.text: Observe two shelter intake days only with consent, free supervised training and no lost pay
Apply after 2031 coding loss only to still-hiring paid shelter posts with mortgage-covering combined usual income

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell clinics AGI by 2036 reaches code in 2036, with hands-on animal-care robots around 2039. A decade lets us look at paid roles and what retirement would actually cost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think my pay is safe for now, although testing hours may narrow before 2036. I will not guess a pension or use the children’s incomes to make a retirement date look affordable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking reminders with nurses and save 160 monthly while my wage holds. Ava and I would request written retirement statements and the mortgage balance each year. In the first year after 2036, if code ends, I’d seek real paid work; I would retire only if verified income and savings cover housing and everyday costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about later job changes, with bills secure now. Ten years lets us check figures instead of assuming the shelter will always need me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What counts as a paid transition?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask a shelter what paid intake vacancies it filled, not how many people attended a course. A shelter training seat is not the same as a paid job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Ava buy another table?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ava and I would keep her grooming table, not buy a second one on a forecast. Real booked customers would have to come first.

say: I expect **2036 AGI** to reach code before 2039 animal-care robots.
I would judge **retirement resources** from written figures.
think: I expect my **current wage** to hold for now while clinics need checked reminders.
I worry **testing hours** may narrow before the full 2036 change arrives.
do: **Keep** nurse-checked reminders and save 160 monthly while paid.
**Request** annual retirement statements and mortgage balance with Ava.
**Seek** real paid work if code ends after 2036; retire only with verified resources.
feel: **Uneasy** about later hours, with present income secure.
S4.quote: A shelter training seat is not the same as a paid job.
fieldNote: He weighs **filled paid vacancies**, not course attendance, when considering shelter work after a future coding loss.
Retirement requires **documented household resources** against mortgage costs, with no assumed pension or children’s income.

steps.text: Keep checking veterinary reminders with nurses while employed
Save 160 monthly while developer wage holds
Seek real paid openings if code ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my wage could go before I can see a real shelter job. Written terms, eligible income help, and actual paid openings would help. Four months saved buys us a search, not a new salary.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the clinic nurse whether a medicine reminder names the right animal and date. A correct appointment screen can still send a wrong medicine reminder home.

headlineQuote: A correct appointment screen can still send a wrong medicine reminder home.
portrait: Rafael is a **58-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, typical pay and four months saved.
He uses **AI occasionally** on veterinary reminders, with nurse checks and no owner data in prompts.
His wife’s **grooming bookings** vary; his software wage covers most of the mortgage.
He explores **shelter intake** only with free supervised safety training, no lost pay and a real adequate vacancy.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his wage before a real shelter opening is known.
whatWouldHelp: **Written terms**, eligible help and actual paid openings would help.
